structured_output.summary: No confirmed bugs or ship blockers in the D3 optional-hardening diff against 08e2dc2. I found only optional test-coverage gaps. This is a source-trace review; I executed nothing. D3 coverage says nothing about T5 acceptance, and D4, D5 and the real-case work remain open. The message change in R/sem-fit.R:276-282 touches only the refusal text. The `raw_count > 64L` gate and the numeric ledger fields are unchanged. Inferred oracles: 2^40 formats as "1099511627776", 2^60 as "approximately 1152921504606846976", and Inf as "overflow (Inf)".

findings.title: Nested-map refusal is tested for one field and one node only
findings.body: Per-field public tamper (test lines ~134-137) mutates only the stored fit's root `branch_map`. Nested refusal is exercised only through the mocked `.sem_fit_syntax` altering `unique_count` of null:1 (lines ~141-153). Nothing tampers a retained mbco/full or mbco/null node's `branch_map` per field. Nothing tampers a nested child's `branch_map` either. `.sem_valid_outcome` (sem-outcomes.R:213) does enforce the check recursively (sem-outcomes.R:239), so I infer it works, but no test pins it. A regression that skipped map validation on nested nodes would pass this suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a loop over `names(map)` through the mocked `.sem_fit_syntax` (one field per iteration, `out$outcome$branch_map[[field]] <- "forged"`). Also inject a map into a nested branch child. In both cases assert `medfit_sem_unresolved` and `rejected_evidence`.

findings.title: Message-format oracles skip the 2^53 boundary and non-power-of-two counts
findings.body: The R/sem-fit.R:276-282 message path is pinned only at 128L, 2^40, 2^60 and Inf. The exact `2^53` boundary (not labeled approximate) is unpinned, as are counts just above it. So are non-power-of-two products such as 3^k, where `digits = 22` formatting of a double that cannot be written exactly could differ by platform. The 2^60 oracle depends on `format()` printing the full exact decimal expansion, which is inferred, not executed.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add a pure unit test of the count formatter at 2^53, 2^53+2 and a large non-power-of-two count, and consider extracting the formatter into a helper.

findings.title: Public fit test depends on a single-start optimizer
findings.body: The new public-fit test uses `n_starts = 1L` through `fit_sem` and `mbco_sem`, and asserts `is.finite(result$p.value)` and f-minimum equality across branches. It also assumes the null node count (`expect_length(nodes, 3L)`) and the ordering `mbco/null:i` follow `paths` order. The owner already flagged the n_starts=1 and random-retry trap in the dependency suites. Convergence of every refit is not a map or propagation property, so the assertions can fail for unrelated optimizer reasons.
findings.recommendation: Seed the test or use a fixture that is known to converge, and keep the p-value assertion separate from the map-propagation assertions.

next_steps: Clause-to-test mapping (test line numbers approximate). Stored-data public map exact oracle: lines ~104-115. Full and null nested maps, IDs mbco/full and mbco/null:i: lines ~121-125. Parent minimum and .sem_valid_outcome: lines ~127-128. Child IDs, parent_id and NULL child map: lines ~131-134.

More mapping. Public tamper per field: lines ~136-139. Child map injection: lines ~141-142. Injected nested-map refusal: lines ~143-154. Finite 2^40, approximate 2^60 and overflow message oracles, unchanged numeric counts and the >64-RAW policy: lines ~87-98.

The forwarded-mock `!is.null(model)` guard (line 144) is scoped to that one mock inside this test_that block through `local_mocked_bindings`. It cannot leak. The over-cap refusal builds its context with a NULL model in `.sem_fit_branches`, not in `.sem_fit_syntax`, so the guard is harmless.

Read: the diff of all five changed files, R/sem-outcomes.R lines 14-64, 135-165 and 190-271, and R/sem-mbco.R lines 120-229. Omitted: the SPEC and PROPOSAL-T5 documents, the D3 closure JSON, the full test file beyond the diff, `.sem_as_semfit`, `.sem_rebase_outcome`, and the dependency and consumer suites. Spec-clause conformance is therefore unreviewed.
